doc.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023

title: Miles Davis, the 'Dingo' sessions and a New York bar encounter
summary: Playing the kid trumpeter in Michel Legrand's 'Dingo', not meeting the ill Miles in the studio, then a brief barside meeting in the Village.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Oh jeez, it’s heaven. It’s heavenly I mean it really was. Wow. I mean I never thought that would happen. And then Miles Davis, another one. I saw him in New York. You know we didn’t get to hang, it was a different situation. That was when I did the album “Dingo” with Miles. Do you know that album? And the story, and he was in the movie you know. And when I did that I had to be some — when you mentioned I had to be somebody you know, Lalo Schifrin — I mean Michel Legrand it was, and I go into the studio to do this and it’s an Australian production. And if you know the movie, I won’t get into it but in the movie he’s in Australia, but there’s a kid in the movie that wants to be a trumpet player and heard Miles play at the airport and wanted to be — and Miles says to him, “Well, you know kid, whenever — if you ever come to New York you can come and sit in with me. So anyhow I was that kid in the movie, the trumpet player. So Michel Legrand says to me, “Chuck come in here, I want you to hear — you have to be this person. So I want you to listen to this.” So he’s playing me this cassette tape of all these different sounds in Australia. Well I’m a golfer and I had been to Australia a few times and I was out playing golf before this all happened you know, a few years before. And I heard all these birds and all these different sounds in Australia that you don’t hear on this continent. And so I had an idea what this kid heard. So that was in my head and I knew that, so I had to be a jazz player but somebody from the Outback that in his head had all these different sounds. So I used, I did a thing where I would open up the spit valve on the tuning slide. And you’d go [scats] with that, ‘cause there’s no center. So you can swim all over the place with that. I kind of put that in there, other different things that I put in as this kid. And I’m on every other track on that album with Miles. But unfortunately Miles was sick, that was when Miles was really getting sick, right before he passed. And he didn’t come in for those sessions. He came in by himself so I didn’t really get to hang with him at all. I wish I could have but I didn’t. And but I did get to run into

him in New York, going back to New York and the Village, and once again it was a very brief meeting. I sat down next to him in a bar, or he came in, I was at the bar. We were in back with the orchestra with Jack Elliott and Allyn Ferguson. And we did it live at Studio 8H in New York. So we got there and got to the Village when we flew in and everything was closing. But we went into this one place, we went into the Brecker Brothers’ club and that was closed. They were all closed already. But this one club in the Village who wanted to have a taste myself and Vince DeRosa on French horn and a few other players. And I’m sitting there, and I was the only one sitting at the bar. I ordered a cognac I think. And next thing I know, next to me is Miles sitting there. And now the interesting thing is I knew that Miles was doing a new album because a dear friend of mine by the name of Doc Lawless, who was also Buddy Rich’s road manager when I was on the band, is the uncle of Hines, Hines & Dad. So he was telling me, he said, “Chuck,” he was my limo driver actually, he drove me there. He had a limo pick us up in New York. So he says to me, he says, “You know, Chuck,” he says, “I’m driving Miles around, he’s doing a new album.” And I said, “Really, how wonderful.” Now Miles is sitting next to me and I said, “Miles, my name is Chuck Findley” and I said, “by the way, I love your new album.” And he says, “How could you? It’s not out yet.” And I was talking about the prior album that he had just released you know. And that was the end of that, he got up and went downstairs to the bathroom and I never saw him again. So anyhow, just meetings like that you know. That’s what he does.
